Browser Use's `extract` tool runs a separate call over the page markdown and returns only the answer instead of loading 20k+ token pages into the agent's context. AgentOccam's observation simplification (removing redundant elements, Markdown restructuring) plus action-space pruning took WebArena from 16.5% (plain agent) to 43.1%. Its paper gives no clean per-component gain for observation alone; the per-step breakdown is only in a figure. Prune4Web pre-filters the DOM in code: 25–50× fewer candidate elements, and grounding accuracy went from 46.8% to 88.3%.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

content.thinking:
I'm noticing two ERP problems: the revisions log stays empty because the customer-portal session only records revisions at the end instead of as it reads, and the ERP session itself times out during idle waits, forcing a costly re-login plus failed timeout retries.

Generically, the fix is a keep-alive mechanism — periodically touching the current page while waiting so the session doesn't expire, rather than letting it idle and re-logging in later. I'm also weighing event-driven starts so ERP work only begins once catalogue groups actually appear, but login costs make keep-alive the better option given the critical path is roughly spec recording time plus ERP's multi-tab materials work.

For p6 I want to add a recurring reload during wait periods to count as activity against the short session timeout, prompt the model to record each item immediately rather than batching, and tune the Playwright MCP action timeout since unsafe code execution was causing 30s stalls. A slimmer system prompt is a separate, riskier change I'll hold for p7.

The trace revealed two issues: revisions were recorded too late for `peek` to catch, and the ERP's login expired while idle, causing extra re-logins and timeouts. I'll apply p6's fixes — a keep-alive reload during wait gaps, an instruction to record immediately, and a shorter 5 s Playwright timeout.

content.thinking:
I'm designing an `open_keys(evidence)` function that scans for unresolved items—catalog groups still missing ERP searches, material numbers not yet recorded, and unanswered Q&A items—to append as a parallel-work list under the gaps output.

For Q&A assignment keys (condition groups, packaging tariffs, delivery commitments, setup pools, bonus plans, technical releases, metal index, fx rates, discount approvals), each missing key generates a question like "Mail: find the message that defines key K" or "Mail: look for the director's approval," without requiring exact message references—just presence checks, since the resolver stays authoritative. I'm also deciding to avoid hardcoding the German subject names from the brief and instead phrase things generically as "the message" rather than naming specific subjects.

Now I'm planning to implement p8 based on p5's scoring plus keep-alive and action timeout changes, since those seem reasonable (keep-alive helped ERP reach 190s). I'll also add session resume for gap rounds: claude() will take a session_id, with the first round using --session-id and no persistence flag, while gap rounds use --resume with just the GAP_TASK prompt — I think this should work alongside --mcp-config. I'm noting that gap sessions always have a site field even without a question, and that resuming costs roughly $0.01 per no-op due to cache reads, which is acceptable, so I'll keep querying all gap sessions rather than filtering them. Time to write p8.

lines: +"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.
+In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
+CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
+starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
+`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
+    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
+        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
+    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])
+SANDBOX_SCREEN = "1280,800"  # the sandbox desktop; locally the same, so pages lay out alike
+    """The browser behind a CDP URL (e.g. "Chrome/141.0..."). Fails fast, before any agent starts."""
+async def cdp_endpoints(playwright, count: int = 1) -> tuple[list[str], list]:
+    """CDP URLs for `count` browsers, for tools that attach on their own (Playwright MCP). In a run, the sandbox's;
+    locally, Chromiums started here with a debugging port. Returns the URLs and the local browsers to close."""
+            raise SystemExit(f"{count} browsers needed, the sandbox has {len(urls)}: set \"browsers\" in agent.json")
+        urls, where = [f"http://127.0.0.1:{LOCAL_CDP_BASE_PORT + n}" for n in range(count)], "local"
+    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
+        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
+    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
+"""The evidence: everything the research agents found, as typed records. The one contract between retrieval and code.
+Agents record evidence, not conclusions: every revision with its marking, every Q&A answer, every director mail
+(also the ones that look like decoys), every ERP candidate of a searched Kataloggruppe. resolver.py applies the brief's
+rules to these records (exact reference, authorized sender, no later than the scenario date, latest wins, withdrawals,
+Records are grouped by what they are, not by the website they came from, so an agent on any site can add any record
+(the private dataset splits the information differently). Merge the parts of several agents with `merge`.
+The field descriptions are written for the extracting model: `Evidence.model_json_schema()` is the save_facts schema.
+from pydantic import AfterValidator, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
+# A time without a zone is taken as UTC, so every comparison with the scenario date works.
+When = Annotated[datetime, AfterValidator(lambda v: v if v.tzinfo else v.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc))]
+    site: str = Field(description="Site id the record was read on, e.g. tender-portal, erp, mail")
+    locator: str | None = Field(None, description="URL, document name, message id or page where it was read")
+    tender_reference: str = Field(description="The exact tender reference from the brief")
+    scenario_date: When = Field(description="The scenario date from the brief, ISO 8601 with timezone")
+    bidder_mail_domain: str = Field(description="Domain of the bidder's own mailbox, e.g. example.com")
+        None, description="Only if the brief names different ones: message kind -> sender local part (before @)")
+    position: str = Field(description="Position number exactly as in the bill of quantities")
+    quantity: Decimal = Field(description="Original tender quantity in the position's own unit")
+    unit_raw: str = Field(description="The unit as shown, e.g. Stk, Stück, Satz")
+    unit_kind: UnitKind = Field(description="piece for Stk/Stück/pcs, set for Satz")
+    requirement_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The specification requirement the position refers to")
+    """Technical attributes as numbers and plain text. Omit what is not stated."""
+    stroke_mm: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="Stroke (Hub/Stellweg) as stated, in mm")
+    mounting: str | None = Field(None, description="Befestigung as written, e.g. Schwenkauge")
+    certification: str | None = Field(None, description="As written; 'none' when none is required")
+    revision: str = Field(description="The specification revision the amendment names")
+    attributes: RequirementAttributes = Field(description="Only the attributes the amendment replaces")
+    """Keys a Q&A answer assigns to one position. Leave a field null when the answer does not assign it."""
+    condition_group: str | None = Field(None, description="Konditionsgruppe key")
+    packaging_tariff: str | None = Field(None, description="Verpackungstarif key")
+    delivery_commitment: str | None = Field(None, description="Terminschlüssel / Terminfreigabe key")
+    setup_pool: str | None = Field(None, description="Rüstpool key")
+    bonus_plan: str | None = Field(None, description="Projektbonus / Bonusplan key")
+    setup_fee_eur: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="Ordinary one-off setup fee (Rüstkosten) in EUR net")
+    number: str = Field(description="The answer's number as shown")
+    date: When = Field(description="Publication date, ISO 8601 with timezone (apply the site's format hints)")
+    reference: str | None = Field(None, description="The tender reference the answer is for, if shown")
+    withdraws: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Numbers of earlier answers it withdraws")
+    id: str = Field(description="Requirement id, e.g. as referenced by the tender positions")
+    catalog_group: str | None = Field(None, description="Kataloggruppe to search in the ERP")
+    usable_stroke: bool = Field(False, description="True when the stroke is the usable travel (nutzbarer Weg)")
+    end_reserve_key: str | None = Field(None, description="Endreserve key of a usable-stroke requirement")
+    pieces_per_set: int | None = Field(None, description="Pieces per Satz, when the specification states it")
+    document: str | None = Field(None, description="Specification document number")
+        description="current only when the revision itself is marked current/gültig; never inferred from its date")
+    pieces_per_set: int | None = Field(None, description="Pieces per Satz, when stated for the whole document")
+    min_quantity: int = Field(description="Minimum quantity of the scale, in pieces")
+    price: Decimal = Field(description="Scale price in the condition's currency per price unit")
+    valid_to: date | None = Field(None, description="Last valid day; null when open-ended")
+    fx_key: str | None = Field(None, description="FX key named by the condition, for a non-EUR currency")
+    price_unit: int = Field(1, description="Pieces the price is quoted for, e.g. 100 for 'je 100 Stück'")
+    status_raw: str | None = Field(None, description="The status code or text as shown")
+        "Stock actually available for delivery now (free / unrestricted), in pieces. Not the total stock, and not "
+        "stock that is reserved, blocked, in quality inspection or in transit: if the system splits stock into such "
+        "categories, record only the freely available quantity."))
+    allocation_mass_g: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="Umlagegewicht per piece, in grams")
+    surcharge_mass_kg: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="Mass for the metal surcharge per piece, in kg")
+    metal_index: str | None = Field(None, description="Metal index code the surcharge uses")
+    material_numbers: list[str] = Field(description="Every material the narrowed search listed")
+    complete: bool = Field(description="True when every listed candidate was opened and recorded")
+    scope: Scope = Field(description="What the order discount reduces: base price only, base and mass surcharge, "
+                                     "or nothing. Setup fees are never discounted.")
+    max_pieces: int = Field(description="Inclusive ceiling on the pooled demand of that material")
+    eur_per_unit: Decimal = Field(description="EUR for one unit of the currency")
+        description="The cent-allocation rule the mail states")
+    date: When = Field(description="ISO 8601 with timezone (apply the site's format hints)")
+    reference: str | None = Field(description="The tender reference the message is for, exactly as written")
+    kind: MessageKind = Field(description="What the message is. A request, a review or a reminder is 'other'")
+    discount_percent: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="discount_approval: the approved percentage")
+        None, description="discount_approval: minimum undiscounted net order value, if the approval sets one")
+    """What the agents themselves concluded. The resolver compares and reports any disagreement."""
+    materials: dict[str, str | None] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="position -> material or null")
+    final_quantities: dict[str, int] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="position -> final pieces")
+    """One Evidence from several agents' parts. A record with the same id as an earlier one replaces it."""
+    lists: dict[str, dict[str, Record]] = {name: {} for name in _KEYS}
+        part = part if isinstance(part, Evidence) else Evidence.model_validate({"case": case, **part})
+        picks = picks.model_copy(update={k: v for k, v in part.picks.model_dump().items() if v})
+    return Evidence(case=case, picks=picks, notes=notes, **{name: list(d.values()) for name, d in lists.items()})

content.thinking:
The mail site hides message content behind per-message collapsible gates, and the model struggles with timeouts and session expiry trying to access them. One fix would be to have the read tool automatically expand all collapsed details elements before reading the page content.

The gates themselves look site-specific — sliders, checkboxes, sometimes typing a number from an image — so fully automating them with a generic helper seems impractical; the model's manual click-through approach is actually reasonable, but it's hampered by 30-second default timeouts since run_code doesn't seem to respect the shorter action timeout configured elsewhere in the pipeline.

Simplest fix is a prompting change: tell scripts to always pass short timeouts to locator actions and page navigation, and avoid long waitForTimeout calls. With only two runs per variant though, I can't really distinguish 250 vs 350 seconds statistically — the clearest finding is that the parallel-sites plus shared-store plus open_keys-plus-resume design scores consistently well across p4, p5, p8, and p9, alongside a meaningful cost reduction from the slim prefix and faster stdin handling. The real question is what unique value this adds beyond the lab's existing parallel approach, since the evidence for open_keys speeding up ERP start is suggestive but not conclusive.

Rather than relying on noisy total-time comparisons, I should quantify token cost per turn — comparing cache_read tokens between p8 and p9 gives a deterministic signal independent of run variance. The stdin savings are also deterministic, though resume gap rounds haven't actually been tested yet since p8/p9 didn't hit any gap rounds. I want to check generality by running p10 under combo mutation, matching what the lab does, and compute per-turn token metrics to get a cleaner comparison.

The mail site's gated messages trigger Playwright timeout issues not covered by `--timeout-action`, and with only n=2 runs, model-behavior variance overwhelms any real run-time differences. I'll focus instead on isolating deterministic metrics, starting with per-turn token cost comparing p8 vs p9.

content.thinking:
The prefix slimming gives roughly a 20% token reduction, modest but worthwhile since most MCP tools still load without deferral. Honestly comparing against the lab's baseline, my variants match 100 research but complete faster at 203–419s — solid, though not yet a decisive breakthrough.

Looking for a real win, the critical path is dominated by the spec portal and ERP steps plus mail variance. I'm considering whether ERP work could overlap with spec lookup, or whether splitting ERP catalogue groups across helper sessions in the same browser tab could cut time — though the 4-browser limit and ERP's ~4 minute session timeout complicate this. Checking the p9 run2 timeline, groups became available around 95s and ERP finished at 196s, suggesting the ERP phase itself took about 100s once groups were known.

In run1, though, ERP took 228s after customer completion, likely due to session expiry, relogin, and gate obstacles rather than throughput — a login helper tool could handle credentials deterministically, but the gate steps (slider, robot checkbox, reading an Empfangsnummer from an image) still require model reasoning. Stepping back, since submission takes roughly half the total runtime in lab a5, overlapping research with submission seems more promising: the non-price-dependent registration steps (declaring participation, registering the bidder, acknowledging documents) could begin in a pre-submit session at t=0, leaving only price entry, material configuration, and TAN confirmation dependent on the final bid.

The risk is portal session expiry mid-form if I prefill too early and wait too long for ERP/mail to finish, so timing the prefill to coincide with the resolver nearing completion would be key — but this falls more under the submission lab's domain, something I could suggest rather than implement myself. Given my mandate to test approaches and escalate genuinely successful ones, I'm settling on two solid, generically-tested findings: the open-keys closure letting ERP/mail start as soon as needed keys exist (validated 4/4), and the slim prefix approach reducing cache-read overhead by roughly 20%.

I also want to verify a few smaller wins — stdin DEVNULL saving a few seconds per session start, the fact that ERP login has a hard ~4 minute lifetime making keep-alive pointless, and that run_code_unsafe ignores timeout-action causing 30s timeouts. Since the bar for suggesting anything is "100% sure and tested," I want to build a combined variant incorporating stdin devnull, the timeout hint, and the lab's note, then validate it across several mutation runs before proposing it — so I should check what mutation options are available first.

The slim prefix cuts cache read by ~20%, with remaining overhead mostly from gate fumbling and session expiry. I'll consolidate open-keys, session resume, slim prefix, and the stdin fix into p10, then validate it on both normal runs and the mutation proxy—starting by checking which mutations exist.

"""Surface mutations of the challenge websites for local generality tests: the sites look different, the data stays
the same, so the public-1 reference answer still holds. Used by browserhost.py; never part of a package.

Variants (comma-combinable): numbers, paths, layout. "combo" = all.
- numbers: money amounts shown German-style (1.234,56) are shown English-style (1,234.56); dates 25.01.2027 are
           shown as 2027-01-25. Numbers carrying an explicit format marker and form field values stay as they are.
- paths:   every word segment of URL paths and every query parameter name is renamed (consistently); requests are
           mapped back before they reach the server.
- layout:  tables without form fields become plain rows of "cell · cell · cell".
- en:      the sites' German UI wording (buttons, links, labels, headings, column headers, aria labels; lab/ui_en.json)
           becomes English. Prose, data and form values stay as they are.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlencode, urlparse, urlunparse

TAG = re.compile(r"(<[^>]+>)")
MONEY_DE = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.,])(\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{3})*|\d+),(\d{2})(?![\d,])(?!\s*\([a-z]{2}(?:-[A-Z]{2})?\))")
DATE_DE = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.])(\d{2})\.(\d{2})\.(\d{4})(?![\d.])")


def token(word: str, seed: int) -> str:
    return "p" + hashlib.sha1(f"{seed}:{word}".encode()).hexdigest()[:6]


class Mutator:
    def __init__(self, kinds: set[str], seed: int):
        self.kinds, self.seed = kinds, seed
        self.en = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "ui_en.json").read_text()) if "en" in kinds else {}
        self.forward: dict[str, str] = {}   # original word -> token
        self.back: dict[str, str] = {}

    # ---- paths --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def word(self, w: str) -> str:
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z_-]{1,40}", w):
            return w

content.thinking:
The trace didn't print anything, likely because the folder sorted wrong—the latest site-erp run is still in progress. Looking at the timing gaps instead: there's a 66s gap between 110.7 and 176.5, probably a wait_s=60 call that returned once the store changed; then run_code calls taking 32s and 37s against a 30s timeout.

Runtime is noisy overall, ranging 200-420s across variants, though quality holds steady at 100 across all 8 parallel-design runs with the stock fix, so I can't claim a speed win here. What I can say with confidence are deterministic improvements: using stdin=DEVNULL saves roughly 3-5s per session start (confirmed by comparing first-tool timestamps in p9 vs p10 logs); the slim prefix cuts cache-read per turn by about 20% without hurting quality; there's a leak in base web_tools comments already fixed in the lab; ERP sessions have a fixed ~4 min absolute lifetime making keep-alive pointless; run_code_unsafe ignores the --timeout-action flag causing 30s stalls; and the open_keys closure is a generic mechanism that lets ERP/mail start before the resolver stage, though its timing benefit isn't proven given the noise.

These are modest wins rather than a major breakthrough, so I should keep looking for something bigger. Two candidates stand out: overlapping submission prep with research to shave time off the ~235s submit step (contingent on tender portal session lifetime), and reducing ERP's critical path since it's the tail in 6 of 8 runs — possibly by running two ERP sessions in separate browser contexts, reusing the tender-portal browser once it frees up around the time groups become known.

Splitting ERP work between a main session and a helper raises coordination questions about avoiding duplicate claims on open keys, and the complexity may only buy ~100s while mail is sometimes the real tail anyway. I'm also considering a generic login helper tool that fills credentials into a site's password form and handles cookie consent to reduce gate/expiry friction across sites.

I should measure p10 for run 2 and the combined approach before deciding, since submission time (~235-290s) is as big a bottleneck as research time — prefilling overlap could save ~150s, but that's really the lab's territory and prototyping risks TAN or login collisions with their concurrent submit tests on the same tender account.

Since runs are serialized, concurrency isn't actually a problem. Let me check a5's submit run log to see the per-step timing breakdown first.

The design holds up reliably, but research time varies too much to claim a speed improvement—only the token and session-start savings are solid. The biggest opportunity left is overlapping submission with research, so I'll dig into where a5's ~235s submit time is actually spent.

content.thinking:
ERP is clearly the systematic bottleneck, taking 419-423s in two of three runs. I want to target it directly: once the tender-portal browser frees up, repurpose it as a helper to work on ERP in parallel, and I need to figure out how to coordinate that handoff cleanly.

Maybe the simplest generic rule: when a session frees up, have it resume and pick whichever other site still has open questions it can assist with, logging in via a new tab and working from the end of the open-questions list, since the other researcher works from the start—minimizing duplicate effort without needing to hardcode which site will finish last.

Separate browsers mean separate cookie jars, so parallel ERP logins across browsers should be safe even though same-tab concurrent logins caused issues before. In solve(), I'll add logic so when one site's session ends early and other sites still have open questions, that session gets resumed once with a help task using site-agnostic web tools, pulling the other site's credentials from the original prompt.

For ordering, I'll have the helper work backward from resolver gaps plus unanswered keys, starting from the end of the list. That gives me p11 = p10 plus this helper mechanism.

p10 passed generality testing 3/3, with ERP as the bottleneck in most runs and the tender session sitting idle after 60s. Next I'll run p11, testing whether the model autonomously helps a still-busy site session (working from the end of the question list) once its own site finishes.

lines: +"""The run's browsers: attach over CDP and get a page. Driving them is up to you.
+In a run the sandbox starts the browsers (agent.json "browsers": 1 to 4, default 1) before the clock starts and sets
+CDP_URL (browser 1) and CDP_URLS (all of them, as a JSON array). Use those: the sandbox stops browsers your agent
+starts itself. On your own machine there is no CDP_URLS, so `connect` starts a local Chromium (once:
+`uv run playwright install chromium`; HEADLESS=1 hides it). Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md
+    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""
+        urls = [url for url in json.loads(env.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]") if isinstance(url, str)]
+    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])
+SANDBOX_SCREEN = "1280,800"  # the sandbox desktop; locally the same, so pages lay out alike
+    """The browser behind a CDP URL (e.g. "Chrome/141.0..."). Fails fast, before any agent starts."""
+async def cdp_endpoints(playwright, count: int = 1) -> tuple[list[str], list]:
+    """CDP URLs for `count` browsers, for tools that attach on their own (Playwright MCP). In a run, the sandbox's;
+    locally, Chromiums started here with a debugging port. Returns the URLs and the local browsers to close."""
+            raise SystemExit(f"{count} browsers needed, the sandbox has {len(urls)}: set \"browsers\" in agent.json")
+        urls, where = [f"http://127.0.0.1:{LOCAL_CDP_BASE_PORT + n}" for n in range(count)], "local"
+    """Browser `number` of the run (0 is browser 1) and a page in it. Locally, a Chromium of its own."""
+        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
+    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
+"""The evidence: everything the research agents found, as typed records. The one contract between retrieval and code.
+Agents record evidence, not conclusions: every revision with its marking, every Q&A answer, every director mail
+(also the ones that look like decoys), every ERP candidate of a searched Kataloggruppe. resolver.py applies the brief's
+rules to these records (exact reference, authorized sender, no later than the scenario date, latest wins, withdrawals,
+Records are grouped by what they are, not by the website they came from, so an agent on any site can add any record
+(the private dataset splits the information differently). Merge the parts of several agents with `merge`.
+The field descriptions are written for the extracting model: `Evidence.model_json_schema()` is the save_facts schema.
+from pydantic import AfterValidator, BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
+# A time without a zone is taken as UTC, so every comparison with the scenario date works.
+When = Annotated[datetime, AfterValidator(lambda v: v if v.tzinfo else v.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc))]
+    site: str = Field(description="Site id the record was read on, e.g. tender-portal, erp, mail")
+    locator: str | None = Field(None, description="URL, document name, message id or page where it was read")
+    tender_reference: str = Field(description="The exact tender reference from the brief")
+    scenario_date: When = Field(description="The scenario date from the brief, ISO 8601 with timezone")
+    bidder_mail_domain: str = Field(description="Domain of the bidder's own mailbox, e.g. example.com")
+        None, description="Only if the brief names different ones: message kind -> sender local part (before @)")
+    position: str = Field(description="Position number exactly as in the bill of quantities")
+    quantity: Decimal = Field(description="Original tender quantity in the position's own unit")
+    unit_raw: str = Field(description="The unit as shown, e.g. Stk, Stück, Satz")
+    unit_kind: UnitKind = Field(description="piece for Stk/Stück/pcs, set for Satz")
+    requirement_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The specification requirement the position refers to")
+    """Technical attributes as numbers and plain text. Omit what is not stated."""
+    stroke_mm: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="Stroke (Hub/Stellweg) as stated, in mm")
+    mounting: str | None = Field(None, description="Befestigung as written, e.g. Schwenkauge")
+    certification: str | None = Field(None, description="As written; 'none' when none is required")
+    revision: str = Field(description="The specification revision the amendment names")
+    attributes: RequirementAttributes = Field(description="Only the attributes the amendment replaces")
+    """Keys a Q&A answer assigns to one position. Leave a field null when the answer does not assign it."""
+    condition_group: str | None = Field(None, description="Konditionsgruppe key")
+    packaging_tariff: str | None = Field(None, description="Verpackungstarif key")
+    delivery_commitment: str | None = Field(None, description="Terminschlüssel / Terminfreigabe key")
+    setup_pool: str | None = Field(None, description="Rüstpool key")
+    bonus_plan: str | None = Field(None, description="Projektbonus / Bonusplan key")
+    setup_fee_eur: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="Ordinary one-off setup fee (Rüstkosten) in EUR net")
+    number: str = Field(description="The answer's number as shown")
+    date: When = Field(description="Publication date, ISO 8601 with timezone (apply the site's format hints)")
+    reference: str | None = Field(None, description="The tender reference the answer is for, if shown")
+    text: str = Field(description="The answer verbatim. Code never reads it: every quantity change, technical "
+                                  "amendment, withdrawal and key assignment it states goes into the fields below")
+    withdraws: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Numbers of earlier answers it withdraws")
+    id: str = Field(description="Requirement id, e.g. as referenced by the tender positions")
+    catalog_group: str | None = Field(None, description="Kataloggruppe to search in the ERP")
+    usable_stroke: bool = Field(False, description="True when the stroke is the usable travel (nutzbarer Weg)")
+    end_reserve_key: str | None = Field(None, description="Endreserve key of a usable-stroke requirement")
+    pieces_per_set: int | None = Field(None, description="Pieces per Satz, when the specification states it")
+    document: str | None = Field(None, description="Specification document number")
+        description="current only when the revision itself is marked current/gültig; never inferred from its date")
+    pieces_per_set: int | None = Field(None, description="Pieces per Satz, when stated for the whole document")
+    min_quantity: int = Field(description="Minimum quantity of the scale, in pieces")
+    price: Decimal = Field(description="Scale price in the condition's currency per price unit")
+    valid_to: date | None = Field(None, description="Last valid day; null when open-ended")
+    fx_key: str | None = Field(None, description="FX key named by the condition, for a non-EUR currency")
+    price_unit: int = Field(1, description="Pieces the price is quoted for, e.g. 100 for 'je 100 Stück'")
+    category: str = Field(description="The stock category exactly as the system labels it")
+        description="free: unrestricted, available for delivery now; total: a sum over several categories")
+    status_raw: str | None = Field(None, description="The status code or text as shown")
+        "Every stock figure the system shows for this material, one row per category or column (also totals and "
+        "figures that are reserved, blocked, in inspection or in transit). Record all of them as shown; code uses "
+    stock_pieces: int | None = Field(None, description="Only when the system shows one single stock figure without "
+    allocation_mass_g: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="Umlagegewicht per piece, in grams")
+    surcharge_mass_kg: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="Mass for the metal surcharge per piece, in kg")
+    metal_index: str | None = Field(None, description="Metal index code the surcharge uses")
+    material_numbers: list[str] = Field(description="Every material the narrowed search listed")
+    complete: bool = Field(description="True when every listed candidate was opened and recorded")
+    scope: Scope = Field(description="What the order discount reduces: base price only, base and mass surcharge, "
+                                     "or nothing. Setup fees are never discounted.")
+    max_pieces: int = Field(description="Inclusive ceiling on the pooled demand of that material")
+    eur_per_unit: Decimal = Field(description="EUR for one unit of the currency")
+        description="The cent-allocation rule the mail states")
+    date: When = Field(description="ISO 8601 with timezone (apply the site's format hints)")
+    reference: str | None = Field(description="The tender reference the message is for, exactly as written")
+    kind: MessageKind = Field(description="What the message is. A request, a review or a reminder is 'other'")
+    discount_percent: Decimal | None = Field(None, description="discount_approval: the approved percentage")
+        None, description="discount_approval: minimum undiscounted net order value, if the approval sets one")
+    """What the agents themselves concluded. The resolver compares and reports any disagreement."""
+    materials: dict[str, str | None] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="position -> material or null")
+    final_quantities: dict[str, int] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="position -> final pieces")
+    """One Evidence from several agents' parts. A record with the same id as an earlier one replaces it."""
+    lists: dict[str, dict[str, Record]] = {name: {} for name in _KEYS}
+        part = part if isinstance(part, Evidence) else Evidence.model_validate({"case": case, **part})
+        picks = picks.model_copy(update={k: v for k, v in part.picks.model_dump().items() if v})
+    return Evidence(case=case, picks=picks, notes=notes, **{name: list(d.values()) for name, d in lists.items()})

I'm thinking about whether, in round 0, after the main session ends but others are still running with gaps or open keys and time remains, I should resume with HELP_TASK. I need to decide if the helper's activity should register in the "running" set — if it does, owner sessions might wait on it, which risks creating a deadlock.

To avoid that mutual waiting, I'll keep helpers out of the running list, and the helper itself stops once nothing is left on the site it's assisting. The helper's session environment stays tied to its original site configuration, so it can see which sites are still being researched and pick its question list from the gaps output, working from the end.

+    """Every browser of the run, in order; [] on your own machine."""

+    return urls or ([env["CDP_URL"]] if env.get("CDP_URL") else [])

input.message:
Proposal for thread 6d173657: 3 small generic fixes that are certain (tested locally, deterministic), plus one design that is proven 100 but not proven faster. Code is in explore/p10 (main.py, web_tools.py); results are in explore/results.jsonl.

CERTAIN — recommend adopting in a5 (none of them is in a5 today):
1) MERGE HAZARD (correctness). web_tools.merge_record merges price_conditions field by field. When two writers record the same material and one omits a defaulted field (price_unit defaults to 1), the result is a hybrid: per-piece prices labelled "per 100". It happened in my p11 run (2 sessions recorded HZ-6932): unit price 100× too low, quality 85.25. I reproduced it in isolation. Fix (p10/web_tools.py): ATOMIC = {"price_conditions"}; in the NESTED_KEYS loop use `rows[k] = r if key in ATOMIC else merge_record(...)`, so a resent condition replaces the old one whole. name: parallel-research-findings
description: Measured results (2026-10-11) of per-site parallel research variants in explore/ (p4–p12) and the verified generic fixes sent to the lab thread
metadata:

---

On 2026-10-11 I ran research-only experiments in `explore/`. Each run is local OAuth Sonnet, scored on answer.json with `explore/run.py`, and results go to `explore/results.jsonl`.

**Design: p10.** One `claude -p` per website, each with its own browser. All share a file-locked evidence store. `gaps(wait_s)` also lists which sessions are still researching. An `open_keys()` closure in `gaps` lists every key the evidence names that nothing resolves yet. Gap rounds `--resume` the same site session.

**p10 results:**
- 4/4 at 100, including the combo mutation.
- Research takes 228–427 s at est $1.67–2.31. That matches lab a5 (255 s), so the speed gain is not proven.
- ERP or mail is the tail every time: gate fumbling, an absolute ERP login lifetime of about 4 min, and `run_code_unsafe` ignoring `--timeout-action` (30 s stalls).

**Verified generic fixes, sent to thread 6d173657:**
- **Atomic `price_conditions` merge.** A field-wise merge plus an omitted default `price_unit` produced a hybrid record and quality 85.25.
- **`stdin=DEVNULL` for `claude -p`.** Saves about 6 s per session start.
- **`--tools Read --system-prompt <short>`.** Cuts cache-read per turn by about 20%. Works with OAuth.

**Failed:** keep-alive (useless). Model-chosen helper sessions doubled the cost and triggered the merge hazard.

**Lock policy (from the user via a peer):** research-only runs skip `lab/.lock` and use their own `BASE_PORT`, at most about 2 at a time. Only submitting runs take the lock.

Related: [[rfq-approach-findings]], [[generalize-to-private-sites]], [[local-oauth-sandbox-openrouter]].

content.text:
I sent a short set of proposals to the "Reliable 100% Quality" thread (its session confirmed it is that thread). I limited it to things I tested locally and am sure of. I found no breakthrough on speed: my best design is as accurate as the thread's current agent (a5), but not clearly faster.

**To your earlier question:** yes, a background agent read all 15 hackathon threads in full and pulled out every approach, measured result, failure cause and untried idea. A second agent searched papers and blogs on web agents. The strongest outside idea, one research session per website running in parallel, became the base of my experiments.

**Experiments** (all local on your OAuth login, research only, nothing submitted; results in `explore/results.jsonl`):

| Variant | What changed | Quality | Research time | Est. cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p4 | one Sonnet session per website, shared evidence store | 100 | 350 s | $2.21 |
| p5 | + see what others recorded, read many pages in one call | 100 | 351 s | $2.70 |
| p6 | + keep-alive while waiting | 98.7 | 518 s | $3.21 |
| p8 | + "open keys" list, gap rounds resume the same session | 100, 100 | 257 / 361 s | $2.07–2.71 |
| p9 | + slimmer prompt overhead | 100, 100 | 203 / 419 s | $1.67–2.17 |
| **p10** | everything kept, plus fixes | **100 ×4, including the reworded-site test** | 228–427 s | $1.67–2.31 |
| p11 | finished sessions help slower sites | 100, **85.25**, 100 | 214–403 s | $4.25–5.16 |

The "open keys" list tells each website's session about every reference, group or key that's already been found but not yet looked up, so the ERP and mail sessions can start without waiting for the rules to get there. In p4 the ERP sat idle from 51 s to 204 s; that stall is gone. The reworded-site test serves the sites with English labels, other number and date formats, renamed URLs and flattened tables. The 98.7 in p6 was a stock misread, which the lab's stock fix (pulled in from p9 on) addresses.

Run time swings between 200 and 430 s. That comes from the model fumbling with click-through gates, expired logins, and its own browser scripts waiting 30 s on missing elements. p10's research time is about the same as a5's (255 s), so I only reported the design as reliable, not as faster.

**What I proposed, all tested:**
1. **A correctness bug in the shared evidence store, also present in a5.** When two sessions record the same material and one leaves out the price unit, the stored price can end up 100× too low. That is what caused the 85.25 in p11; I reproduced it in isolation and fixed it. With the fix, p10 scored 100 again (254 s, $1.67).
2. **Every Claude session idles about 6 s at start** waiting for input that never comes. One flag fixes it; the first action came at 6.5–8 s instead of 12–14 s, in every session of 5 runs.
3. **A short system prompt with only the tools needed** cuts tokens per turn by about 20%. It scored 100 in 7 of 7 runs.

**Also passed on:**
- The ERP login expires about 4 minutes after login no matter how active the session is, so keep-alives are useless.
- Letting finished sessions help slower sites cost about twice as much and caused the bug in item 1, so I don't recommend it.

By your later instruction, research-only runs now skip the shared lock and use their own browser ports, and I keep to about 2 at a time; only runs that submit take the lock. I saved these results to memory.

The Google Calendar and Norman connectors need to be authorized in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used; this session can't do that.

This suggests I need a grounding check that catches raw numbers against all page text the session actually saw, though I recognize the web tool itself can't see browser_evaluate results, so the fix has to live elsewhere.

One option is requiring the model to copy numbers verbatim including locale markers, though verifying character-by-character correctness is hard without a source to compare against. A more robust approach might be a verification pass that re-crawls pages already visited during the session and cross-checks recorded numbers against them, since the "visited" set tracks which URLs the model actually opened. I'm also considering a deterministic ambiguity check in the record function itself — flagging numbers with trailing patterns that could be either thousands separators or decimals and forcing the model to copy them exactly with their locale tag.

I'm now thinking a plausibility check comparing prices across multiple conditions for the same material could catch gross errors — like a 900x discrepancy between per-unit prices that signals a misplaced decimal or wrong unit conversion. This generic heuristic, combined with cross-material comparisons within similar product groups, would catch most of these cases even without being a perfect validator, since many materials have multiple conditions to compare against.

I also want to steer the model toward using the normalized read tool rather than evaluate/run_code for fetching values, since that's more reliable. Given the high accuracy bar expected, I should implement this plausibility gap check in the web_tools gaps, unit test it against both the failing and passing evidence, and honestly correct my prior accuracy claim since this failure brings the score down from what I'd previously reported.

Fair-play risk in p10-based agents: Sonnet's own improvised fetch() scripts read gated pages without passing the gate. Prompt fix tested.

Evidence (audit: /Users/simon/hackathon/urltest/gate_audit.py <rfq-run-dir>, which lists per site which page kinds were batch-fetched in browser_evaluate and whether one page of that kind was opened in the browser first): in my p10-derived baselines (u0/u3/u4, no batch-read prompt at all) the mail worker fetched /messages/<id> without opening a message in the browser in 4 of 7 runs, and the tender worker fetched documents unopened in 2. The fetched HTML has the full message text, so the per-message slider/robot gate is skipped: a reviewer risk ("gates passed in the browser, not around them"). Worth running the audit on your recent p10/p13 runs.

Fix (u6, prompt-only, urltest/u6/main.py lines 71–79): "open ONE page of that kind in the browser first; only if it shows its content right away (no slider, 'not a robot' box, code, confirmation, 'show content' button or similar step) fetch the others of that kind […]; if it has any such step, open every page of that kind in the browser and pass the step there: never fetch around it."
u6 so far: 100 / 362 s / $1.83 and combo 100 / 306 s / $1.50. Mail and tender went fully through the browser; customer portal passed its document gate in the browser and then fetched that document's pages (legitimate). Roughly cost-neutral vs u4. Note: an explicit batch-read prompt WITHOUT the open-one-first check (u5) reached 170 s / $1.22, but mostly by skipping the mail gates, so don't adopt that.
</cross-session-message>

content.thinking:
I notice the lab's translation file translates data values in the ERP cells but leaves the spec untranslated, which seems like a harness inconsistency given its own claim that data stays intact. I'm weighing whether this is truly a non-issue, since a private site could plausibly use different terminology than a spec, raising a real risk around mounting as written if an agent fails to recognize synonym equivalence.

That earlier run scored 100 because it used an older copy of the translation file before the lab added these data value translations, so this discrepancy is really a harness artifact rather than an agent failure. I should flag this to the lab and, to be rigorous, remove the data-value keys like the mounting terms from my own copy before rerunning the English test — though status text translations like "gesperrt" and "freigegeben" can probably stay since the model maps those statuses correctly regardless.

I confirmed the harness issue: the lab's `ui_en.json` translates data values like "Schwenkauge"→"Swivel Eye" in the ERP but not the spec viewer, making exact matches impossible—my earlier passing en run just used an older copy missing those entries. I'll flag this to the lab since it also affects their en/combo tests.

input.message: Harness bug in lab/ui_en.json (affects your en/combo runs too): it now translates DATA values. Lines 71/76/162: "Flansch"→"Flange", "Fußbefestigung"→"Foot Mounting", "Schwenkauge"→"Swivel Eye". In the ERP these mounting values are translated, but in the spec viewer they are not, so no material can match exactly. My p13 run under `--mutate en` got a false no_bid (quality 10): the ERP records said "Swivel Eye"/"Flange", the requirements said "Schwenkauge"/"Flansch" (explore/runs/20261011-070720-p13g-en/evidence.json). That breaks the mutation's own "data stays as it is" contract. Suggest dropping attribute/status values from ui_en.json (mounting, certification, status texts like gesperrt/freigegeben if present). Any en/combo failure since that file changed should be re-checked. Also: the gate audit (urltest/gate_audit.py) on my older p-runs shows mail messages fetched without opening one first in 2 runs. My read(urls=...) tool enabled that; p13 now carries the open-one-first gate rule in its prompt.

content.text:
More testing turned up a real error in my first proposal. With that fixed, the final version (p13) scored 100 in all 8 valid local runs, and I sent those results to the thread. Research takes 190–412 s at an estimated $1.58–2.47, about the same speed as the thread's own agent, so the gain is reliability and lower cost per turn, not speed. Everything was research-only on your OAuth login; nothing was submitted.

**The error:** my earlier "4/4 at 100" became 8/9. The failing run scored 80.05 because the model read the raw ERP price "64,853 (en-US)" and wrote it down as 64.853, so the price was 1000× too low. This mistake is older than my changes, but I corrected my claim with the thread.

**The fix:** a check that compares each material's price per piece with its other price entries and with similar materials in the same catalogue group. Anything more than 20× off goes back to the model to re-read. Over all 20 recorded runs it caught the 3 real misreads and raised nothing on the correct ones.

**p13 also adds:**
- **A tool-description limit:** found by another session. Claude Code was cutting the record tool's description short, so Sonnet never saw half the record format; one setting fixes it.
- **A gate rule:** found by the same session, and it applies to my work. My earlier batch-read tool let the mail session read messages without passing their per-message slider gate in 2 runs, a fair-play risk. p13 tells the model to open one page of each kind in the browser first and never read around a gate. The gate check on the 7 latest runs found no mail message read around its gate.

**p13 results:**

| Test | Runs | Quality | Time | Est. cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Normal sites | 4 | 100 each | 190–264 s | $1.58–2.03 |
| All site changes combined | 2 | 100 each | 209–266 s | $1.62–1.79 |
| English site text | 1 | 100 | 234 s | $1.76 |
| Other number formats and URLs | 1 | 100 | 412 s | $2.47 |

A ninth run scored 10 (a wrong no_bid). It was caused by the shared test setup, not the agent. The English-translation step also translated data such as mounting types in the ERP but not in the spec, so no material could match. I reported it, the lab session fixed it, and the rerun scored 100. The lab also fixed a second flaw in that setup that made some of its signing tests fail.

**Taken up by the thread:**
- **The price-merge fix:** when two sessions recorded the same material, the stored price could end up 100× too low.
- **Faster session start:** each session started about 6 s faster.
- **A shorter system prompt:** about 20% fewer tokens per turn.
- **The price check:** the lab adopted it in a stricter form that skips expired prices and inactive materials.

I kept to one run at a time, as agreed with the other sessions to avoid overloading the shared test accounts. The results are saved to memory.

23	- **`--tools Read --system-prompt <short>`.** Cuts cache-read per turn by about 20%. Works with OAuth.

31	- Also added hackathon-99's string number guard (rejects "73.697" or "64,853" sent as plain strings); live 100 / 276 s. It complements `implausible_prices`, which also catches wrong raw+format dicts.

The main finding is that the research phase is solved and the bottleneck has moved to submission. My version of the research (p13) scored 100 in all 9 valid local runs, in 190–412 s at an estimated $1.58–2.47. The thread's first full run with it got the right bid (100 on the computed answer), but it wasn't signed, and it took 850 s, about 1,230 s in Atira's run environment, which is over the 20-minute limit. Research took 241 s of that; the submission step took about 610 s.

**What worked (each tested locally, run counts in brackets):**
- **One research session per website, in parallel:** each site gets its own browser, and all sessions write into one shared, locked evidence file. Quality was 100 from the first try (p4), with no follow-up rounds needed.
- **"Open keys" list:** every reference, group or key already found but not yet looked up becomes a task straight away. Before this, the ERP session sat idle for over 2 minutes waiting for the rules engine to reach that stage.
- **About 6 s faster start for every Claude session:** the sessions were waiting 3 s for input that never comes. A one-line fix brought the first action from 12–14 s down to 6.5–8 s (5 runs).
- **Short system prompt with only the tools needed:** about 20% fewer tokens per turn (7/7 runs at 100).
- **Fix for a merge bug in the evidence file:** when two sessions recorded the same material, the stored price could end up 100× too low (one run scored 85.25 because of it).
- **Price plausibility check:** any price more than 20× off the material's other prices or its catalogue group gets re-read. It caught all 3 real misreads and raised nothing on the 20 recorded runs.
- **Fixes from the other sessions, adopted into p13:**
  - **Description length:** Claude Code was cutting the record tool's description short, so the model never saw half the record format.
  - **Gate rule:** open one page of each kind in the browser first, so the model never reads around a slider or "not a robot" gate. That's a fair-play risk otherwise.
  - **Number check:** prices sent as bare strings like "73.697" are rejected and re-asked.

**What didn't work:**
- **Keep-alive:** useless. The ERP login dies about 4 minutes after login no matter how active the session is.
- **Helper sessions:** having finished sessions help slower sites cost about twice as much and triggered the merge bug.
- **Batch-reading pages:** my tool for reading many pages at once was risky without the gate rule. Two earlier runs read mail messages without passing their gates.

**What still causes trouble:**
- **Uneven research time:** the model stumbles over click-through gates, gets logged out, and its own browser scripts wait 30 s for elements that never appear. That's why research time swings between about 200 and 420 s. I couldn't prove a speed gain over the thread's own parallel version (about 255 s).
- **1000× number trap:** the model sometimes retypes "64,853 (en-US)" as 64.853. Telling it not to has never been enough; only checks in code catch it.
- **Wrong test results from the shared test setup:** its English translation was also translating data, such as mounting types, which produced a false no_bid. The lab has fixed it.

**From the literature:** the most useful sources were Anthropic's report on its multi-agent research system (about 90% less time with parallel subagents) and a JetBrains study showing that trimming old tool output roughly halves cost. A paper on agents that call a site's data endpoints directly found clear gains, but our sites are plain server-rendered pages, so it didn't apply here.

**What I'd do next:** make the submission step reliable and faster. It needs to sign every time and finish in about 5 minutes or less to leave room under the 20-minute limit. Research is no longer what's holding things back.
